title: Using Artificial Intelligence Tools in Digital Marketing: A Survey Study of a Number of Private Sector Banks in Iraq
abstract: This research aims to explore the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in digital marketing. A questionnaire was developed to confirm the relationship between the research variables. Using a sampling methodology, 384 questionnaires were distributed to private sector banks in Nineveh Governorate, and the data were analyzed using SPSS version 24. The research results revealed a knowledge gap regarding the nature of the relationship between AI and digital marketing, and confirmed a statistical relationship between the research variables. Therefore, the banks included in the study need to enhance the role of AI in digital marketing. This research is the first of its kind to integrate current variables (AI and digital marketing) into a single hypothetical model for Iraqi private sector banks. The research findings can be utilized to implement AI in digital marketing, increasing banks' opportunities to achieve their goals and objectives. Consequently, private banks should organize training courses for their departments and participate in training courses with other banks. Keywords: Artificial intelligence; Digital marketing; Attraction; Engagement; Learning; Retention; Communication.

title: Domain-Adaptive Probability Distribution Theory
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to probability distribution theory centered around the concept of "domain adaptation." Traditional methods often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their applicability to a specific dataset. We propose a dynamic distribution window mechanism that adapts the distribution parameters based on the unique characteristics of the input data, thereby enhancing model prediction accuracy and generalization. The core claim is that this approach allows for more intelligent and robust model training compared to static distribution theory.

title: 量子机器学习的基于自适应损失函数设计
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) is a rapidly evolving field of artificial intelligence that leverages the principles of quantum mechanics to enhance machine learning algorithms. This paper presents a novel quantum machine learning algorithm, termed "Adaptive Loss Function Design" (ALFD), focusing on dynamically adjusting loss functions to optimize model performance and achieve more precise predictions. Traditional loss functions often suffer from suboptimal performance and limited adaptability, while QML offers the potential for significantly improved learning efficiency and accuracy through the inherent capabilities of quantum systems. ALFD employs a self-adjusting mechanism that iteratively modifies the loss function based on data fluctuations, creating a continuous optimization process. The core mechanism leverages quantum entanglement and superposition to efficiently explore the loss function space, leading to enhanced model generalization and predictive capabilities. This paper provides a detailed analysis of ALFD, including its mathematical formulation, implementation details, and experimental results demonstrating its superior performance compared to traditional loss functions and existing QML algorithms. The advantages of this approach lie in its adaptability, potentially leading to more robust and accurate models across diverse datasets.

title: Neurogenesis Reinforcement Learning Language Model
abstract: We propose the Neurogenesis Reinforcement Learning Language Model (NRLLM), a research framework in which stable linguistic mastery can trigger endogenous growth of a language agent trained through reinforcement learning. Godrick is the proposed experimental realization. Its defining hypothesis is that an exactly-one-neuron increase in a dynamic hidden structure, conditioned on independently specified mastery criteria, can support subsequent learning without sacrificing previously acquired capabilities. The framework separates content admission, learning, mastery assessment, and structural growth. A beta discernment subsystem evaluates whether authorized material is relevant and sufficiently supported for a target linguistic capability; it does not certify mastery. A future continual-learning stage would use a localhost chat and explicitly permitted internet sources. We formalize a candidate growth gate, outline initialization and plasticity choices, and specify controlled comparisons against fixed capacity, alternative growth triggers, replay, and feature replacement. Earlier work establishes individual components, including one-unit growth, artificial neurogenesis, reinforcement learning, and language-model expansion. The contribution claimed here is a proposed synthesis and falsifiable experimental protocol, not demonstrated superiority or an established claim of historical priority. No implementation results or benchmark measurements are reported.

title: 基于动态几何结构的自适应优化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on dynamic geometric structures, designed to adaptively adjust optimization parameters and automatically refine optimization strategies based on data distribution and target variables. The core mechanism involves mapping system parameters to a dynamic geometric space, simulating data distribution changes through geometric transformations, and optimizing parameters to achieve superior results. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of quantitative experiments, showcasing its ability to outperform traditional optimization methods in various scenarios. The algorithm's adaptability and self-tuning capabilities offer a significant advantage in complex optimization problems.

title: Non-Linear Geometric Error Correction via Quantum Algorithms
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum algorithm for non-linear geometric error correction, designed to enhance the accuracy and reliability of quantum computation. Traditional geometric error correction methods often struggle with the complexities of subtle errors, limiting the potential of quantum systems. This research explores the application of quantum entanglement to achieve a fundamentally different approach to error detection and correction. The core mechanism leverages quantum entanglement to create a global state synchronization and entanglement, enabling a robust and efficient error correction process. The developed algorithm demonstrates significant improvements in error detection and correction compared to existing classical methods, particularly in scenarios involving complex geometric transformations. We present a detailed analysis of the algorithm's performance, including mathematical formulations and experimental validation. This work contributes to the advancement of quantum error correction and opens avenues for more reliable and robust quantum computation.

title: Title: Geometric Complexity Measures for Machine Learning Models
abstract: This paper investigates the use of geometric complexity measures to enhance the robustness assessment of machine learning models. Traditional metrics, while valuable, often fail to capture the intricate relationships within the model's representation. We introduce a novel set of geometric properties – curvature, torsion, and connectivity – designed to go beyond standard metrics by identifying vulnerabilities and patterns inherent in model structure. The core mechanism involves quantifying these properties using novel mathematical constructs and rigorously evaluating their impact on model performance across diverse datasets. The goal is to develop a more comprehensive and insightful assessment of model resilience, contributing to improved model design and stability.

title: Title: Quantum-Enhanced Wave Function Optimization (QWWO)
abstract: Quantum-Enhanced Wave Function Optimization (QWWO) presents a novel approach to accelerating the optimization of wave function configurations, specifically within the realm of quantum chemistry. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with the computational complexity of exploring vast solution spaces. This paper introduces QWWO, a framework that employs quantum-enhanced state preparation and measurement to dramatically reduce the search time and improve the efficiency of finding optimal configurations within complex quantum chemical calculations. We detail the algorithm's core mechanism, highlighting the critical role of quantum entanglement and superposition in enabling this acceleration. This work explores the potential of leveraging quantum phenomena to overcome limitations in current optimization techniques, offering a promising pathway towards more efficient and rapid solution discovery.

title: Context-Aware Federated Learning with Differential Privacy
abstract: Federated learning (FL) offers a promising approach to training machine learning models on decentralized data sources without direct data sharing. However, traditional FL models often operate under the assumption of homogeneous data distributions, which frequently doesn't hold true in real-world scenarios. This research investigates a novel framework for context-aware federated learning that addresses this limitation by integrating local contextual information alongside differential privacy mechanisms. The core claim is that incorporating context allows for more accurate model aggregation, while differential privacy safeguards user data. The proposed system designs a federated learning architecture that dynamically adjusts model updates based on device-specific context and employs differential privacy to mitigate privacy risks. We demonstrate the potential of this combined approach to achieve higher model accuracy and enhanced privacy protection compared to standard FL methods. This work contributes to a more robust and practical distributed learning paradigm suitable for diverse and heterogeneous data environments.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning with Temporal Logic for Robotics
abstract: This paper proposes a novel neuro-symbolic framework for robotics, leveraging the strengths of both neural networks and temporal logic to address the persistent challenge of complex robotic task execution. Current robotic systems frequently encounter difficulties when confronted with tasks demanding intricate reasoning, often relying heavily on hand-engineered rules and struggling to adapt to unexpected changes in the environment. Our approach aims to overcome this limitation by integrating neural networks for perceptual processing – capable of robustly handling noisy and ambiguous sensory data – with temporal logic for symbolic reasoning – allowing for precise temporal planning and constraint satisfaction. The system is designed to learn from data while maintaining the rigor and expressiveness of logical formalisms. We introduce a specific architecture that allows for continuous learning and refinement of both the neural components and the temporal logic rules. The core of our methodology relies on a mechanism for translating perceptual observations into temporal logic formulas and, conversely, executing temporal logic plans to guide robot actions. We explore the potential of this hybrid approach in scenarios requiring coordinated actions over time, demonstrating improved performance compared to purely neural or purely symbolic solutions. The presented framework offers a pathway towards more adaptable, robust, and intelligent robots capable of tackling complex, real-world tasks.

title: Dynamic Bayesian Networks for Modeling Complex Biological Systems
abstract: This paper proposes the utilization of Dynamic Bayesian Networks (DBNs) as a powerful tool for modeling complex biological systems, addressing the limitations of static Bayesian Networks in capturing the dynamic nature of these systems. Static networks struggle to represent the temporal evolution of biological processes, which are inherently characterized by state transitions and dependencies over time. The core of this approach involves constructing DBNs that explicitly model these temporal dependencies. These DBNs are further enhanced by integrating stochastic differential equations (SDEs) and hidden Markov models (HMMs) to represent the underlying probabilistic dynamics. The resulting models offer a more realistic and nuanced representation of biological systems, allowing for improved analysis of complex interactions and predictions of future states. The key innovation lies in the specific design of a DBN architecture tailored for the intricacies of biological modeling. This approach provides a framework for understanding how biological systems evolve and respond to external stimuli.

title: Quantum Computing-Based Topological Entropy Calculation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum computing approach to calculate topological entropy, leveraging quantum entanglement and superposition to efficiently determine the complexity of topological systems. Traditional entropy calculation methods are limited by computational complexity, particularly for high-dimensional topological systems. Our approach utilizes quantum circuits to simulate the topological states and employs entropy information to characterize the system's properties. This offers a significant improvement in computational efficiency and provides a new perspective on topological data analysis, potentially unlocking insights into the fundamental behavior of these intricate structures.

abstract: LACF – Visualisation Structurelle(Architecture de Contrôle Formel pour Systèmes LLM)DescriptionCe dépôt constitue la divulgation publique et horodatée de l’architecture LACF (Logical Architecture for Controlled Flow / Architecture Logique de Contrôle Formel).L’architecture a pour objet d’isoler complètement un modèle de langage probabiliste (LLM) au sein d’un système de sécurité à confiance nulle (Zero-Trust), en interdisant toute interaction directe ou auto-attribution de privilèges.Principes structurels fondamentaux : Isolation totale du Cœur LLM (Air-Gap / Coupe-Feu Mathématique)Le modèle probabiliste est encapsulé dans un environnement hors-ligne (SAS Zero-Trust) contrôlé exclusivement par un vérificateur formel basé sur le solveur SMT Z3. title: Generative AI and adaptive systems for customising help-seeking scaffolds: A systematic review
abstract: Abstract Help-seeking is a central self-regulated learning (SRL) process; however, generic scaffolds often misalign with learners’ heterogeneous needs. This systematic review addresses the lack of consolidated evidence on how artificial intelligence (AI), including large language models (LLMs), customises help-seeking scaffolds, the effects thereof, and the methodological and ethical constraints. Guided by SRL theory, this review examined empirical studies on AI-driven customised help-seeking support, focusing on evidence availability, comparative impacts versus standard scaffolds, evaluation approaches, and reported gaps. Database searches (IEEE Xplore, Web of Science, ERIC, and ScienceDirect) conducted on 28 May 2025 yielded 3,576 records; blinded multi-reviewer screening in Rayyan following PRISMA procedures identified 31 eligible studies for narrative synthesis. Data extraction by three reviewers showed high raw agreement (87.3%) but low chance-corrected agreement (Cohen’s κ ≈ 0.05; Fleiss’ κ ≈ 0.17), resolved via structured adjudication and full consensus. The included interventions (2017–2025) ranged from rule-based intelligent tutoring and learning-analytics dashboards to LLM-based textbooks, writing feedback, laboratory guidance, and coding assistants, enabling conversational, intent-sensitive, on-demand scaffolding. Most studies reported improved academic performance and engagement, particularly for lower-performing or lower–prior knowledge learners, although null or mixed effects and inconsistent satisfaction outcomes were common. The recurrent limitations concerned sample scope, duration, measurement heterogeneity, usability, and risks related to hallucinations, bias, privacy, equity, and overreliance. The review concludes that although AI-customised help-seeking scaffolds are promising, they are context-dependent and delineate methodological and design priorities to advance SRL-aligned, responsible AI support for help-seeking.

title: FSAN: Flow State Attention Network for Aerodynamic Prediction
abstract: Accurate aerodynamic prediction is critical for designing fuel-efficient and safe transportation systems such as aircraft and automobiles, yet traditional computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations remain computationally expensive and expertise-intensive, severely limiting their use in iterative design and real-time analysis. Existing deep learning surrogates suffer from two major limitations: (i) they are evaluated on datasets with narrow flow-condition ranges, leaving their performance under complex flow conditions undemonstrated; (ii) they treat global flow conditions as a single vector injected uniformly across all surface points, ignoring that different geometric regions experience distinct local flow phenomena, which degrades prediction accuracy under complex flow conditions. To address these limitations, we propose the Flow State Attention Network (FSAN). FSAN separately encodes point cloud and flow conditions, then partitions the geometry into multiple flow states via learnable soft assignments, and uses flow features to update these state representations, which in turn influence point cloud features through state changes. This enables fine-grained, state-specific interaction between geometry and flow information. Extensive experiments on two well-recognized aerodynamic benchmarks demonstrate that FSAN achieves the highest accuracy among the methods compared in this work at a higher computational cost. On Emmi-Wing, FSAN reduces the Relative L2 (REL-L2) error by over 20\% compared to the strongest baseline (Transolver), and on DrivAerNet++, it achieves a 10\% reduction compared to the strongest baseline (AdaField). These results establish FSAN as a promising neural surrogate on public benchmarks with diverse flow conditions and geometries.

title: From Reading Code to Reading Spec: A Verified Layer for LLM-Driven Codebase Maintenance
abstract: The rapid growth of LLM-generated code increases software complexity and the maintenance burden on engineers. While LLMs offer a potential automated alternative, this structural complexity hinders their ability to manage codebases directly. We introduce the Provable Representation Of Original Functionality (PROOF), which manages codebases indirectly via structured specifications. To enable full-lifecycle codebase management strictly through these specifications, PROOF abstracts codebase topology into a hierarchical natural-language representation. To establish absolute trust, the system proves semantic equivalence by reconstructing source code exclusively from this specification. This verified foundation drives maintenance requests, executing code modifications while synchronously updating itself to prevent semantic drift. Experiments on real-world repositories confirm the effectiveness of these specifications.

title: A Fast Non-Iterative Method for Learning Latent Variable Causal Models
abstract: Latent variable causal models provide a powerful framework for describing causal relationships when the variables of interest are not directly observable. A fundamental challenge in learning such models is to identify both the measurement model, which associates observed variables with latent variables, and the causal structure governing the latent variables. Existing approaches often rely on constraint-based procedures or computationally demanding gradientbased iterative optimization over discrete measurement structures and continuous model parameters, limiting their applicability to large-scale problems. In this work, we propose a non-iterative approach for learning the graphical structures of latent variable causal models. The first step of the proposed method provably recovers the measurement model from observed data using a low-rank subspace identification and clustering procedure. To overcome the difficulty of further inferring the latent causal graph, the second step of the proposed method is capable of approximating the covariance matrix of the latent variable based on a matrix-valued aggregation function. The recovered latent covariance matrix is subsequently used for causal discovery at the latent-variable level effectively. The resulting framework decomposes the problem into two stages, and such separation avoids the need to jointly optimize the measurement structure and the latent causal graph and enables the learning procedures to be performed in the typically lower-dimensional latent space. We provide theoretical analysis of the proposed framework and empirically evaluate its ability to recover latent causal structures under different measurement and causal configurations. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and computational efficiency of the proposed approach.

title: Title: Bayesian Geometric Chaos for Optimal Algorithm Design
abstract: This paper explores the application of Bayesian Geometric Chaos to optimize algorithm design. The core idea centers on creating a probabilistic Bayesian framework that dynamically refines algorithm parameters during execution, guided by a measure of "chaos" – a concept representing unpredictable variability and sensitivity to initial conditions. Traditional optimization methods often employ fixed parameter settings, limiting the potential for discovery. This work proposes a novel approach that leverages Bayesian inference to iteratively adjust algorithm parameters based on observed outcomes, effectively incorporating randomness and uncertainty into the optimization process. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this framework through a series of illustrative examples, showcasing its ability to navigate complex optimization landscapes and potentially generate more robust and efficient algorithm designs. This research moves beyond static optimization by introducing a dynamic and probabilistic element, offering a fundamentally different perspective on algorithm design.

title: 基于量子纠缠的自适应搜索算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive search algorithm based on quantum entanglement, designed to optimize complex search spaces and significantly enhance search efficiency. Traditional search algorithms often rely on random exploration, limiting their effectiveness. This work leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to create a mechanism that facilitates more efficient search operations. The core of this approach involves the manipulation of entangled states to guide the search process, resulting in improved performance across various search scenarios. The paper details the fundamental principles, the proposed algorithm's architecture, and its experimental validation, demonstrating the potential of this method to address limitations in current search techniques.

title: 异质性信息理论的自适应计算范式
abstract: This paper introduces a novel computational paradigm, termed "Adaptive Information Theory Computing Paradigm" (AITCP), predicated on the principles of Heterogeneity Information Theory (HIT). AITCP dynamically adjusts the computational process based on the inherent heterogeneity of input data, leading to improved efficiency and robustness. We explore the fundamental concepts of HIT and demonstrate its practical application within a simulated data processing framework. The paper presents a detailed algorithmic framework for implementing AITCP, outlining its key components and illustrating its potential impact across various computational tasks. We highlight the advantages of this approach compared to traditional methods, emphasizing its adaptability to complex, non-stationary data distributions. The research contributes to the advancement of adaptive computation and offers a promising pathway towards more efficient and resilient algorithms.

title: 基于动态网络的表征与智能决策
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to representing and analyzing complex systems using dynamic network architectures. We propose a method that dynamically adjusts node and edge weights based on environmental feedback and system state learning, enabling automated network structure optimization. The core mechanism involves building a dynamic network model, employing iterative learning to adjust network parameters, and integrating intelligent decision-making algorithms to guide this adjustment process. This offers a significant advancement over static network models, particularly in scenarios requiring rapid adaptation to changing conditions. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulated examples, illustrating improved performance in dynamic systems and highlighting the benefits of automated network structure refinement.

title: Probability Distribution Dynamic Adjustment and Algorithm Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the application of dynamic probability distribution adjustment as a novel optimization strategy for machine learning models. Traditional machine learning algorithms often rely on fixed, pre-defined probability distributions, limiting their adaptability to dynamic environments. We propose a new approach that dynamically adjusts these distributions based on real-time data and environmental feedback, aiming to improve model generalization and robustness. The core mechanism centers around an adaptive probability distribution update system that leverages historical data and feedback to avoid over-fitting. This work explores the potential benefits of this approach in various machine learning scenarios, including classification and regression tasks. The paper presents a conceptual framework and preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of this dynamic distribution adjustment method.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Wavefunction Collapse for Time-Dependent Systems
abstract: Abstract: Quantum-enhanced wavefunction collapse for time-dependent systems aims to accelerate the collapse of wavefunction states, offering a potential breakthrough in simulating complex dynamics. This paper explores a novel method leveraging quantum algorithms to directly manipulate the wave function, significantly reducing the time required for collapse compared to traditional approaches. We detail the core mechanism, outlining the algorithm's structure and its potential to address limitations in current simulation techniques. This work represents a fundamental shift in our understanding of wavefunction dynamics, potentially unlocking new capabilities for modeling complex systems.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Deep Learning Model
abstract: This paper introduces a novel deep learning model based on quantum entanglement, aiming to enhance both learning efficiency and generalization capability. Traditional deep learning models are inherently limited by the computational power of classical computers. This work explores the potential of leveraging quantum entanglement to overcome these limitations, proposing a new architecture that harnesses the unique properties of entangled particles to accelerate training and improve model robustness. We detail the core mechanism of this approach, outlining its theoretical underpinnings and preliminary experimental validation. The paper concludes with a discussion of the challenges and future directions for this research.

title: Quantum Entangled Graphs for Optimization
abstract: Quantum entangled graphs (QEG) offer a promising approach to quantum computation, leveraging the unique properties of entanglement to enhance algorithm efficiency and performance. This paper proposes a novel optimization algorithm, "Adaptive Quantum Process Optimization," (AQPO) designed to effectively optimize QEG's design. AQPO utilizes dynamic adjustment of quantum process parameters to control the output of the entangled graph, resulting in enhanced quantum computation performance. The core mechanism of the algorithm focuses on a continuous, iterative process of adjusting quantum process parameters to achieve optimal graph design. We present a theoretical framework and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of AQPO in optimizing QEG designs, highlighting its potential to significantly improve quantum computations.

title: Title: Adaptive Wavefunction Collapse Mapping
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative algorithm for quantum system manipulation, focused on dynamically adjusting wavefunction collapse to generate complex patterns. Traditional quantum algorithms often rely on fixed parameters, limiting the ability to create intricate designs. We propose a novel system of parameters that iteratively adjusts the collapse of wavefunction states, providing a mechanism for creating complex and diverse states. This dynamic system allows for exploration of a wider range of possibilities than static approaches, offering the potential for significantly enhanced design space and pattern generation. The core claim is that this algorithm facilitates the creation of complex patterns through adaptive wavefunction collapse.

title: Title: Non-Local Quantum State Synchronization (NQSS)
abstract: Quantum state synchronization is a critical challenge in quantum information processing, demanding precise coordination between multiple quantum systems. Existing synchronization techniques often struggle with long-distance synchronization, hindering the development of complex quantum algorithms. This paper introduces the Non-Local Quantum State Synchronization (NQSS) framework, proposing a novel method leveraging entanglement-based synchronization to overcome distance limitations. We detail the core mechanism involving a dynamically adjusted entanglement matrix, demonstrating its effectiveness through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation. The proposed NQSS approach offers a significant step forward in achieving robust and scalable synchronization capabilities for quantum systems.

title: Title: Adaptive Quantum Error Mitigation using Entanglement Transfer
abstract: Quantum computing promises revolutionary advancements, but inherent fragility necessitates robust error mitigation strategies. Current methods often require extensive error correction, which is computationally demanding and limits scalability. This paper proposes an innovative adaptive quantum error mitigation technique centered around entanglement transfer, offering a potentially transformative shift from traditional methods. We detail a mechanism designed to rapidly and effectively transfer entanglement across qubits upon detection of errors, effectively propagating correction signals and substantially reducing the burden of error correction. The core claim is that this approach allows for a more efficient and scalable mitigation strategy, eliminating the need for full-scale error correction in many scenarios. This research explores the mathematical foundations of this technique, providing a comprehensive analysis and demonstrating its effectiveness through simulation and preliminary experimental validation. We highlight the potential of this approach to unlock the true power of quantum computation.

title: Temporal Stream Reasoning Based on Biological Neuron Models
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neural network design by leveraging the dynamic behavior of biological neurons. Traditional artificial neural networks operate on static representations, often failing to capture the intricate temporal dependencies inherent in biological systems. This work introduces a framework for constructing more realistic and potentially more efficient neural networks through the simulation of neuronal time streams. The core of the method utilizes differential equation systems to model the complex dynamics within neuronal populations, encompassing synaptic plasticity, ion channel activity, and neuronal interactions. The ability to incorporate time-dependent processes fundamentally shifts the paradigm, allowing networks to learn and represent temporal patterns directly, rather than relying solely on spatial arrangements of connections. The simulation results demonstrate the potential of this approach to achieve greater accuracy and efficiency in learning tasks that rely on temporal information. This research moves beyond static network architectures, offering a biologically inspired methodology for neural computation.

abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to quantum hardware testing and debugging utilizing a multi-agent collaborative system. The core claim is that leveraging the strengths of multiple autonomous agents dramatically improves the efficiency and accuracy of quantum hardware verification. The proposed mechanism involves constructing a system where diverse agents, each specialized in a particular aspect of testing and debugging, operate in concert. This approach addresses the inherent challenges of quantum hardware testing, which often rely on manual intervention, leading to increased time, cost, and potential for human error. The system's architecture incorporates agents for control pulse optimization, error characterization, state tomography, and automated calibration. Mathematical formulations are presented to describe the agents' decision-making processes and the overall system dynamics. The research demonstrates the potential for automated quantum hardware testing and debugging, ultimately contributing to the development of more reliable and robust quantum computing platforms. The system's performance is evaluated through simulated scenarios, showcasing its ability to significantly reduce testing time and improve the accuracy of hardware characterization.

title: Neuromorphic Spiking Neural Networks with Reservoir Computing for Time Series Forecasting
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) augmented with Reservoir Computing (RC) for time series forecasting. Traditional SNNs struggle with the complexities inherent in forecasting tasks, primarily due to the challenges of training and efficiently encoding temporal dependencies. This work proposes a novel architecture where an SNN's recurrent reservoir acts as a non-linear transformation, effectively mapping input time series into a high-dimensional state space. A linear readout layer then processes this state space, leveraging backpropagation through time (BPTT) for training. The key innovation lies in explicitly tailoring the RC framework within an SNN to directly address the requirements of time series forecasting, offering a potentially more efficient and biologically plausible approach compared to existing methods. The core claim is that standard SNNs lack efficient solutions for this task, and the proposed mechanism, utilizing a randomly connected recurrent reservoir, provides a viable pathway for improved performance. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and a conceptual framework, outlining the design considerations and training strategies. This work lays the groundwork for future research exploring the practical implementation and optimization of SNN-based RC systems for real-world time series forecasting scenarios.

title: A Discrete Recovery Failure Mode in Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization Carries Chemically Predictive Information
abstract: A previous report (Okuda, Zenodo DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22469203) identified a discrete failure mode in sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD): at low shot counts, classical configuration recovery can lock onto a reproducible but incorrect "wrong attractor," and injecting a single correct configuration into the raw sample can trigger a discrete escape from it. That finding was established on a shallow circuit (N2, CAS(6,6), 166 two-qubit gates) where the wrong-attractor structure itself was directly observable. Here we address two questions left open by that work. First, was the original demonstration merely a sample-size artifact rather than evidence that the specific injected configuration mattered? We answer this with a controlled random-injection experiment (Fe2S2, CAS(12,12), 2053 two-qubit gates, 76-80 independent trials per condition): recovery probability rises from 14.5% with no injection to 100.0% with one pre-specified escape configuration, while a random single-configuration injection of the same size produces only 15.0% recovery, and the escape itself is discrete while the residual energy error continues to improve smoothly with further injected configurations. Second, at circuit depths beyond roughly 1000 two-qubit gates, the wrong-attractor structure itself often becomes too noise-dominated to observe directly, so a practical recovery procedure cannot simply look for and inject "the" known wrong-attractor escape configuration. We present such a procedure: a small set of chemically motivated candidate configurations is generated and injected, and the best candidate is selected using one of three answer-free criteria (variational energy, escape rate from a known baseline attractor, or seed-to-seed energy variance), chosen by a cheap upfront classification of the target system. Across 23 independent hardware-data trials spanning two IBM Quantum backends and 21 distinct molecular systems and active-space combinations, this decision rule selected the correct candidate in all 23 trials, including one case improving accuracy by approximately 1000x. We report this as validation of the decision framework across a broad range of hardware and chemical conditions, not as evidence of answer-free prediction for arbitrary, genuinely unknown multi-reference chemistry, and report the framework's limitations candidly. Open-source implementation: https://github.com/okudat9/escape-config-predictor

title: Graph-Based Semantic Parsing with Attention-Weighted Relational Reasoning
abstract: Semantic parsing aims to transform natural language sentences into formal logical representations, a critical step in enabling machines to understand and reason about human language. This work proposes a novel approach to semantic parsing that leverages graph-based representation and attention-weighted relational reasoning. The core idea is to represent a sentence's structure as a graph, where nodes denote phrases and edges signify relationships between them. An attention mechanism is then employed to dynamically assign weights to these relationships, prioritizing those most relevant to the task at hand. This approach allows the system to capture contextual nuances and improve the accuracy of logical form construction. We demonstrate that this combination significantly enhances semantic parsing performance compared to traditional methods. The primary formula used within this paper is: *f(s_1, s_2, ..., s_K) = L*, where *f* represents the parsing function, *s_1, s_2, ..., s_K* are the input sentence components, and *L* is the resulting logical form. The attention weights are represented as *α_i*, where *i* indexes the relational edges, and these weights are calculated based on the context and the specific parsing goal. The overall system can be summarized by the equation: *Logical Form = Attention(Graph, Goal)*. This method avoids the limitations of purely symbolic approaches and offers a more flexible and adaptive solution for semantic parsing.

title: Title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Topological Topology Sorting Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel topological topology sorting algorithm based on quantum entanglement. The algorithm leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to efficiently identify and rank topological structures, ultimately enhancing computational efficiency and providing deeper insights into topological phenomena. The core mechanism centers on utilizing entanglement to rapidly assess the structure of a given topological space, allowing for a streamlined and highly effective sorting process. This approach offers a fundamentally different perspective on topological analysis, potentially revolutionizing computational methods and our understanding of complex topological systems.

title: Quantum Error Correction Coding and Synergistic Optimization of Topological Quantum Computers
abstract: This paper investigates the synergistic optimization between quantum error correction (QEC) coding schemes and topological quantum computers (TQC). The core claim is that a deep integration of QEC strategies with the physical topology of TQC can achieve enhanced quantum bit (qubit) error resilience and computational efficiency. The proposed mechanism leverages the inherent topological error correction properties of TQC, designing tailored QEC codes and simultaneously optimizing the topological structure to amplify error detection and correction capabilities. The research addresses a critical gap in the field by moving beyond conventional QEC approaches, which are not directly applicable to the unique characteristics of TQC. The work explores novel methods for maximizing the performance of TQC by considering the interplay between code design and topological architecture. Ultimately, this research contributes to a pathway towards building more robust and efficient quantum computers based on topological principles.

title: Assessing Covariate-Informed Grid Load Forecasting with a Time-Series Foundation Model
abstract: Modern power systems are growing increasingly complex as they integrate diverse generation sources to meet rising demand, making accurate load forecasting challenging. Recent advances in time-series foundation models (TSFMs) resulted in promising performance in zero-shot univariate load forecasting tasks. However, real-world load forecasting often involves multiple target variables and requires the integration of exogenous variables, raising important questions about the utility of TSFMs in realistic settings. In this study, we position Chronos-2, a recently developed model by Amazon, as a representative multi-channel TSFM that supports univariate, multivariate, and covariate-informed forecasting, and conduct a systematic investigation of how such models can be used for real-world load forecasting. While prior work has evaluated Chronos-2 on a limited number of energy-related tasks in a zero-shot setting, its performance relative to established task-specific deep learning models and its behavior when adapted using task-specific historical data remains insufficiently understood. In this work, we evaluate Chronos-2 on two real-world utility datasets, ISO New England and ENTSO-E, and benchmark it against widely used task-specific deep learning models. Our results show that Chronos-2 benefits substantially from task-specific fine-tuning and achieves strong short-horizon forecasting performance, but its zero-shot accuracy lags behind task-specific models and its forecasting error grows more rapidly with increasing forecast steps. Overall, this study provides a detailed characterization of the strengths and limitations of TSFMs such as Chronos-2 in grid load forecasting and offers practical insights into how a pretrained TSFM can be effectively adapted for operational load forecasting applications.

title: Measurement-Device Placement in MDI-QKD Networks with Minimal Trusted Relays
abstract: Measurement-Device-Independent Quantum Key Distribution (MDI-QKD) removes detector side-channel vulnerabilities by delegating measurements to an untrusted relay that, when shared by several user pairs, acts as a Bell-state measurement (BSM) hub. Channel loss still limits the reach of MDI-QKD links, so long-range services rely on trusted relays for key forwarding. As MDI-QKD moves toward metropolitan deployment, a key network-planning question arises: how should BSM hubs be placed on existing fiber infrastructure to minimize the use of trusted relays? In this work, we formalize this challenge as the MDI-QKD Hub Deployment (MHD) problem. We first prove that the MHD problem is NP-hard, and then formulate it as a Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP). To the best of our knowledge, this is the first formulation for MDI-QKD network planning that captures the structural features specific to MDI-QKD, namely a shared BSM hub, two-link user-to-hub routing, and loss-balancing constraints, while jointly determining hub placement, user-to-hub assignment, and trusted-relay demand allocation. Our solution accounts for realistic budget and capacity constraints, including practical insights from real-world deployments of commercial MDI-QKD solutions. Numerical evaluations on three metropolitan topologies (12 to 50 nodes) at realistic geographic distances show that topology structure governs trusted-relay demand: hub placement alone eliminates all trusted relays in compact urban meshes, while in sparse topologies, relaxing the loss-balancing constraint removes the dominant source of trusted-relay usage at no additional infrastructure cost. The key-rate threshold at which trusted relays first appear shifts monotonically with the network diameter, i.e., the largest shortest-path distance between any node pair in fiber kilometers, delineating the feasibility boundary of pure MDI-QKD deployment.

title: Generating radio continuum survey maps of arbitrary size with latent diffusion models
abstract: Radio surveys provide exponentially increasing amounts of observational data, which requires the development of novel data reduction and analysis methods. To this end, realistic simulations of observational data provide controlled environments for testing and developing new methods. Diffusion models excel at synthesizing realistic image data, but are limited by size constraints and high computational demands. We implemented a latent diffusion model (LDM) to synthesize realistic radio survey map cutouts. Further, we developed a technique for sampling radio survey maps of arbitrary size with the LDM. This is done by sampling in multiple sequential steps, whereby consistency is provided through context vectors and image inpainting. We trained our model on observations from the LOFAR telescope obtained from the third data release of the LOFAR Two-Metre Sky Survey. We implemented a LDM composed of a vector-quantized variational autoencoder and a diffusion model operating on the resulting latent representations. We added information on source locations, brightness and sizes by extracting parameters from the public source catalog and encoding them into a vector format passed as context to the LDM. We trained the model for image inpainting to facilitate continuous sequential sampling. We were able to generate realistic cutouts of 512 pixel side length, corresponding to ~5.7 arcmin, with precise control over source locations and brightness. Control over source extension was achieved at lower precision. Sampling of arbitrary-sized maps was made possible, showing realistic results with seamless combination of individual samples and limited only by occasional sampling artifacts.

title: Recovering Weak Signals with Normalizing Flows
abstract: In many scientific disciplines, weak signals of interest are obscured by dominant nuisance signals that are several orders of magnitude stronger. Recovering these weak signals requires subtracting the dominant ones; however, this calibration process inherently distorts or partially suppresses the underlying signal of interest. To address this problem, we propose the use of normalizing flow models to reconstruct calibration-affected weak signals. By leveraging the statistical invariance of the target signals and assuming minimal initial suppression, our framework effectively recovers the lost signal components. We provide a comprehensive theoretical overview of this normalizing flow-based recovery method and demonstrate its efficacy using simulated data.

title: Minimal codes from down-sets of F_p^m violating the Ashikhmin–Barg bound
abstract: The code is written from the definitions in the paper alone — the down-set, D_2 = F_p^2 minus the two lines, and nu(x) = |{y in D_2 : x.y = 0}| — and uses exact integer and rational arithmetic throughout; no code of the authors is used. It supports the statement in Section 1 that every computation is an exhaustive enumeration, and it documents the counterexamples to Corollary 3.6. code/op5core.py — shared core: D_2 and D enumerated point by point, the p+1 projective classes, nu and its spectrum, the closed forms |D_2| = pA − B and nu(1,t), the weights of Lemma 3.1, omega_min and omega_max from eq:ratio (d = |D_2|(p−1)/p kept exact), and the test pomega_min < (p−1)*omega_max. Python 3.8+, standard library only. code/check_F1_F2.py — Lemma 3.1 and eq:ratio against full codeword enumeration (ten cases, p in {5,7,13}, m in {3,4}), and Lemma 3.2 for all legal (delta, eps) at p in {5,7,11}. Output in results/F1_weights_ratio.csv and results/F2_strips.csv: no mismatch. code/check_F3_F4_F5.py — Propositions 3.3–3.4 and Theorem 3.5 over p in {5,7,11,13} with deficits up to 5 (results/F3F4_nu.csv, no violation), followed by a search for counterexamples to Corollary 3.6. results/F5_cor36_counterexamples.txt — 21 counterexamples among the 1516 triples satisfying the hypotheses of Corollary 3.6; the smallest is (delta_1,delta_2; eps_1,eps_2) = (3,7;5,5) at p = 11, where nu_max = 10 < 11 = 2delta_1 + eps_2 and yet omega_min/omega_max = 67/74 < 10/11. The hypothesis 0 < B + delta_1 <= p restores the statement; equivalently the criterion reads nu_max >= 2delta_1 + eps_2 − ceil((B+delta_1)/p) + 1. code/check_F7.py — Theorem 3.11 (minimality iff delta_1 >= 1 and eps_2 >= 1), tested by support inclusion over all pairs of non-proportional codewords, on ten parameter sets (results/F7_minimality.csv): the criterion holds in all of them. code/check_F19_F20.py — the two numerical claims of the open-problems paragraph and the sweep of Remark 4.8. results/F19_open_problems.csv: for (2,3;4,2) one has nu_max = 4 only at p = 5, and 5 for every larger prime tested; for (1,7;5,1) the ratio equals 10/11 at p = 11 and is strictly below (p−1)/p for every p >= 13, the opposite of what the paper states. results/F20_sweep.csv: recounting over 1 <= delta_i, eps_i <= 12 and 11 <= p <= 23 gives 673 shapes violating the bound for every admissible prime (2186 for at least one), against the 1105 and 579 quoted in Remark 4.8; also note that |D_2| = p*A − B is linear in p for every shape, so that qualifier needs a definition. results/verdicts.csv — log of the machine-checked review: one row per submitted claim, with the verdict of the verifier. results/all_local_results.json — raw output of the twenty checks F1–F20. code/run_all.py — runs every check and rewrites results/ in about one minute. Reproduce with python code/run_all.py (standard library only; run under Python 3.13 on Windows).

title: 基于自适应的动态概率模型
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to probabilistic modeling, termed the "Adaptive Dynamic Probability Model" (ADPM), which leverages a self-adaptive parameter adjustment mechanism to optimize model performance in dynamic environments. The ADPM dynamically adjusts model parameters and learning strategies based on input data and model predictions, resulting in enhanced prediction accuracy compared to traditional probabilistic models. We detail the core mechanism, presenting a framework for continuous parameter refinement and learning. The paper explores the benefits of this approach in scenarios requiring adaptability and robust performance across a range of data types. The core claim is that the ADPM provides a significant improvement in prediction accuracy through dynamic parameter adaptation.

abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum algorithm optimization utilizing an adaptive parameter adjustment strategy. This work introduces a dynamically adjusting parameter scheme designed to automatically refine quantum circuit parameters, leading to improved algorithm performance and stability. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulations and analyses, showcasing significant enhancements in convergence speed and fidelity compared to existing static optimization methods. The proposed strategy offers a promising pathway towards more efficient quantum computation.

title: Title: Algorithmic Quantum State Collapse with Adaptive Resonance
abstract: Quantum state collapse is a fundamental process in quantum mechanics, representing the irreversible transformation of a quantum system from one state to another. It's a key challenge in quantum information processing and quantum computing, driving the need for efficient collapse protocols. Traditional methods often struggle with maximizing information preservation during collapse, leading to inefficiencies and potential errors. This paper introduces an algorithmic framework, termed Adaptive Resonance Collapse (ARC), designed to mitigate these issues by dynamically adjusting the quantum system's 'tuning' based on the information content of the collapse event. We demonstrate that ARC significantly improves the fidelity of collapse while reducing the information loss associated with the process, offering a novel approach to enhancing quantum state fidelity. This work explores the use of adaptive resonance – a technique inspired by the brain's neurophysiological mechanisms – to optimize the collapse process, resulting in a more robust and efficient collapse algorithm.

abstract: This paper investigates a novel dynamic topology approach for neural network architectures, aiming to automatically optimize network design based on observed training data dynamics. Traditional neural network architectures are often fixed, limiting their adaptability to diverse learning tasks. We propose a system that dynamically adjusts the connection patterns and layer arrangements, leveraging observed data to iteratively refine the network's structure. This work introduces a mechanism for real-time topology modification, offering a significant improvement over static architectures in terms of learning efficiency and performance across various datasets. The core principle is to create a continuous feedback loop, adjusting the network's topology based on the data's inherent patterns.

title: FADE-RIPE: A Robust Quantum Optimal Control Algorithm for Superconducting Transmons with Realistic Hardware Constraints (reference implementation)
abstract: FADE-RIPE: Transmon Quantum-Gate Optimizer FADE-RIPE (Fidelity Aware, Distortion-aware, Environment-conscious Robust Iterative Pulse Engineering) is a gradient-based quantum optimal control method for a single-qubit gate on a 4-level (N=4) transmon, benchmarked against GRAPE and CRAB (via qutip_qtrl). The model and optimizer include: Realistic transmon physics: An N=4 Hilbert space with Kerr/anharmonic H0, a subspace-projected 2x2 target gate, and an explicit penalty for population leaking into levels |2>, |3>. Exact Lindbladian propagation and gradient: Piecewise-constant Lindblad master-equation propagation with an exact analytic gradient (via the augmented-generator/Frechet-derivative trick). AWG bandwidth filter: A Butterworth low-pass filter on the control pulses, represented as an exact linear operator so the gradient chain rule through it is exact. Filter-function noise penalty: A numerical filter function F(omega) of the optimized pulse, penalized against a 1/f (flux) or thermal-photon power spectral density via an overlap integral. Thermal initial-state fidelity: As-built fidelity optimizations starting from a Boltzmann-weighted thermal state rather than the pure ground state. This upload contains the reference implementation fade_realistic.py, which includes the physics model, optimizer, baseline comparisons, and the analysis/plotting pipeline used for the simulations reported in the companion paper.

title: Core Claim: Design a dynamic adjustment algorithm for quantum entanglement-based hidden variables, leveraging the unique properties of hidden variables to achieve automatic data distribution learning and modeling, and enhance algorithm robustness.
abstract: Quantum entanglement offers a potential paradigm shift in data analysis, offering capabilities exceeding classical methods. This research explores the application of dynamic adjustment algorithms for quantum entanglement-based hidden variables. The core idea revolves around utilizing the inherent properties of hidden variables – their capacity to influence data distribution – to automate the learning and modeling process. The presented algorithm employs an adaptive approach, dynamically adjusting parameters to optimize data distribution based on observed patterns. This approach contrasts with traditional methods that rely on pre-defined parameters, promising enhanced robustness and adaptability. The study investigates the potential of this dynamic adjustment to improve the performance of quantum entanglement-based algorithms across diverse data distributions. The implementation focuses on optimizing a specific metric – data fidelity – by iteratively refining the algorithm's parameters. This research aims to establish a foundational framework for harnessing the power of hidden variables to achieve more efficient and reliable data analysis in the quantum realm.

title: Decentralized Learning with Byzantine Fault Tolerance using Consensus-Based Neural Networks
abstract: This paper explores the feasibility and design of decentralized learning systems capable of Byzantine fault tolerance. The core challenge lies in training neural networks across a distributed network where some nodes may be compromised and actively attempting to disrupt the learning process – a scenario known as Byzantine fault tolerance. We propose a consensus-based neural network training algorithm that leverages a voting mechanism to achieve agreement on model parameters despite the presence of malicious actors. This approach allows for robust learning even when a significant portion of the network is corrupted. The system is designed to tolerate a certain level of Byzantine failures without compromising the accuracy or convergence of the trained model. We formalize the algorithm using mathematical notation and demonstrate its theoretical properties, focusing on convergence and fault tolerance. The key contributions of this work are the detailed specification of the consensus protocol and its integration with a distributed neural network training process.

title: Probability Form Semantic Networks (PFSSNs)
abstract: This paper introduces Probability Form Semantic Networks (PFSSNs), a novel approach to semantic network representation and reasoning. The core claim is that semantic network nodes and edges should no longer be treated as discrete values, but rather as probability distributions, representing the fuzzy associations between concepts. This work leverages Bayesian networks as the underlying mechanism to model these relationships, enabling probabilistic inference and effectively handling the inherent uncertainty in semantic data. PFSSNs provide a more robust and flexible framework for semantic reasoning compared to traditional semantic networks that rely on discrete representations. The proposed method addresses the limitations of existing approaches by incorporating probabilistic modeling, allowing for a nuanced understanding of concept interrelationships and facilitating more accurate and reliable semantic inference. This work demonstrates the potential of PFSSNs for applications requiring robust reasoning under conditions of uncertainty.

title: Automated Theorem Proving for Hardware Security Protocols
abstract: This paper explores the application of automated theorem proving (ATP) to the rigorous verification of hardware security protocols. Current security verification methods often rely on manual analysis, which is prone to human error and struggles to scale with increasingly complex protocols. We propose a novel approach that leverages ATP systems to formally model and verify the correctness of these protocols. The core mechanism involves translating protocol specifications into formal logic statements and then employing an ATP engine to automatically deduce whether the protocol satisfies its intended security properties. This approach offers a reliable, scalable, and potentially more exhaustive method for identifying vulnerabilities compared to traditional approaches. We outline the key steps involved, highlighting the challenges and potential benefits of this paradigm shift in hardware security verification. This work contributes to the development of more robust and trustworthy hardware security systems. ---

title: Emergent Code Generation and Evolution
abstract: This paper explores the concept of emergent code generation through the application of evolutionary algorithms, specifically genetic algorithms. The core idea is to leverage the principles of biological evolution to automatically produce code snippets with complex functionality and optimized performance. Unlike traditional code generation methods that rely on predefined rules or templates, this approach employs a dynamic process where code fragments are treated as 'genes' and subjected to evolutionary operations such as crossover and mutation. The resulting code evolves iteratively, guided by predefined performance metrics. We demonstrate a framework where code snippets are evaluated based on specified criteria, with fitter snippets being selected for reproduction and further modification. This process facilitates the discovery of novel code structures and optimization strategies that might be difficult to conceive through conventional design methods. The key innovation lies in the ability to explore the vast design space of code solutions in a self-organizing manner, leading to emergent behaviors and solutions. The paper outlines the proposed methodology and highlights the potential of this approach for automating software development and optimization tasks.

title: Title: Spatiotemporal Quantum State Synchronization – Wavelet-Based Integration
abstract: Quantum communication relies heavily on the synchronization of quantum states across spatially separated devices. Current methods often struggle with achieving high fidelity and scalability due to complex measurement and synchronization requirements. This paper proposes a novel technique utilizing wavelet-based integration to efficiently synchronize quantum states across spatially separated devices, offering a significant advancement in fidelity and scalability. We introduce a framework where quantum states are integrated using wavelet transforms, allowing for more robust and adaptable synchronization protocols. The core mechanism focuses on exploiting the wavelets' ability to represent complex patterns and efficiently manage the integration process. This approach promises improved fidelity and scalability compared to existing synchronization methods. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our technique through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental results, showcasing its potential for enhancing the reliability of quantum communication systems.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Encoding and Decoding (QIE&D)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to information encoding and decoding, termed Quantum Entanglement Information Encoding and Decoding (QIE&D), leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. The core claim is that QIE&D offers a fundamentally new method for information processing, surpassing the limitations imposed by classical information theory. The underlying mechanism utilizes multi-particle entanglement to construct an encoder-decoder system. The encoding process maps information onto entangled states across multiple quantum particles, while the decoding process extracts the original information through measurements on these entangled states, enhanced by entanglement transformations to improve robustness against noise. QIE&D distinguishes itself from existing quantum information processing techniques by employing multi-body entanglement, providing significantly greater information capacity and processing power. This system is designed to address the challenges associated with long-distance quantum communication and secure quantum computation. The theoretical framework is presented, detailing the key components and operational principles of the QIE&D system. We explore the mathematical formalism underpinning the encoding and decoding processes, focusing on the manipulation of entangled states and the application of entanglement transformations. Furthermore, we analyze the system's sensitivity to various types of noise and propose strategies for mitigating these effects. The potential of QIE&D is significant, offering a pathway toward more efficient and secure information transmission and processing in the quantum realm.

title: Multi-Campus Google Review Analytics Dataset and Reproducibility Package for Service Benchmarking, Domain Generalization, and Reviewer Graph Analysis
abstract: This record provides the processed datasets, supplementary materials, analysis code, frozen data partitions, per-review predictions, result tables, and reproducibility documentation supporting three complementary studies of multi-campus Google reviews. The studies address: (1) aspect-based sentiment analysis and rating–text consistency for cross-campus service benchmarking; (2) imbalanced multilingual sentiment classification under cross-campus domain generalization; and (3) reviewer–campus bipartite graph analysis and reviewer-aware rating aggregation. The frozen corpus contains 6,990 reviews collected from 13 predefined campus listings, including 2,932 reviews with textual content. The sentiment-analysis component includes a 1,200-review human-validated annotation set covering global text sentiment, rating–text consistency, aspect presence, and aspect-level sentiment across eleven service categories. The domain-generalization component provides leakage-controlled frozen partitions, campus-held-out evaluation outputs, and prediction records. The graph-analysis component contains 6,990 reviewer–campus edges, 6,363 pseudonymous reviewer nodes, 13 campus nodes, and all 78 possible campus pairs. Reviewer identities are pseudonymized, and direct profile identifiers and profile images are excluded from the research package. The three analytical tracks are maintained separately to preserve their distinct research questions, units of analysis, and experimental outputs. The package includes documentation describing data provenance, processing decisions, annotation structure, analytical limitations, and reproducibility procedures. This release is version 1.0.0.

title: Field-Adaptive Geometry and Arithmetic Methods – Through Dynamic Learning of Field Features, Automated Construction and Optimization of Geometric-Arithmetic Models
abstract: Field-adaptive geometry and arithmetic methods offer a paradigm shift in modeling, enabling automated construction and optimization of geometric-arithmetic models tailored to specific field characteristics. This paper introduces a novel approach leveraging dynamic learning of field features to automatically adjust model parameters, resulting in improved model accuracy and generalization capabilities. This results in a more flexible and robust system compared to static, fixed models. The work demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach through extensive experiments on diverse geometric and arithmetic datasets, showcasing its ability to achieve state-of-the-art performance.

title: Title: Algorithmic Resonance-Based Quantum Simulation (ARQS)
abstract: This paper introduces Algorithmic Resonance-Based Quantum Simulation (ARQS), a novel quantum simulation algorithm designed to dramatically enhance the fidelity of quantum system simulations through the utilization of resonant frequencies. Traditional quantum simulation methods often struggle with accuracy, particularly for complex systems due to the inherent challenges of representing and manipulating quantum states. ARQS addresses these challenges by exploiting the inherent resonance properties of quantum systems to dynamically adjust simulation parameters, effectively reducing computational cost and error. The core mechanism of ARQS involves identifying resonant frequencies within the system and utilizing them to 'tune' the simulation, leading to a significant improvement in simulation fidelity. This research explores the theoretical foundations, implementation details, and preliminary experimental results supporting the potential of ARQS to revolutionize quantum science.

title: 基于自律的量子计算的熵特征优化
abstract: Quantum computing, a revolutionary paradigm in computation, relies heavily on the stability and reliability of its quantum bits (qubits). Qubit errors are a significant challenge, threatening the accuracy of quantum computations. This paper explores a novel approach to quantum bit optimization utilizing self-regulated quantum computing, focusing on entropy features as a key optimization strategy. We present a framework that dynamically adjusts qubit parameters to minimize error rates, leveraging the inherent properties of self-regulating quantum systems. The research demonstrates a significant improvement in quantum bit fidelity compared to traditional optimization techniques, offering a promising pathway toward robust quantum computation. The core mechanism involves the application of self-regulatory entanglement to guide parameter adjustments, resulting in enhanced error mitigation. The study underscores the critical role of entropy in securing the integrity of quantum information.

title: Quantum-Guided Algorithm for Data Compression (QGDC)
abstract: Quantum-Guided Algorithm for Data Compression (QGDC) is a novel algorithm designed to revolutionize data compression by leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement. This research investigates a quantum-assisted compression technique that focuses on identifying and exploiting subtle statistical correlations within data, offering the potential for significantly improved compression rates and error reduction compared to traditional methods. The core mechanism centers around establishing a 'quantum signature' – a unique quantum state representing the data's statistical characteristics – and utilizing entanglement to accelerate the compression and decompression processes. This paper explores the theoretical underpinnings of QGDC, detailing its architecture, the role of quantum entanglement, and a preliminary assessment of its performance. The results demonstrate a promising level of compression efficiency and error reduction, showcasing the potential of quantum-guided compression.

title: Quantum Entanglement Topological Network Routing
abstract: This paper proposes a novel distributed routing protocol for quantum networks leveraging the topological properties of quantum entanglement. The core idea is to construct a network topology based on entangled states between nodes, enabling communication through the instantaneous correlation inherent in entanglement. This approach aims to overcome the limitations of traditional routing protocols, particularly in terms of speed and security. We define a routing algorithm that dynamically adjusts the entanglement states to facilitate data transmission, effectively creating a network with inherently high bandwidth and resilience to eavesdropping. The algorithm is based on a graph theory framework where nodes represent quantum devices and edges represent entangled pairs. The routing process involves identifying the shortest path through the entanglement network, leveraging the correlated states for rapid information transfer. We explore the mathematical underpinnings of this protocol, outlining key formulas for calculating entanglement metrics, path distances, and routing decisions. The theoretical framework presented here provides a foundation for future research and development in quantum network architecture and routing strategies.

title: Cognitive Landscape Modeling (CLM)
abstract: This paper introduces Cognitive Landscape Modeling (CLM), a novel system for modeling the emergent cognitive landscapes of complex systems. The core claim is that CLM dynamically adjusts the relative importance of different cognitive processes based on environmental input, creating a 'landscape' representation of a system's cognitive activity. We leverage Bayesian inference and agent-based modeling to construct this landscape, enabling a dynamic adaptation of task allocation. CLM offers a departure from traditional cognitive models by focusing on the emergent properties of these cognitive landscapes, providing a more holistic understanding of complex behavior.

title: Causal Bayesian Networks for Anomaly Detection in Complex Systems
abstract: Anomaly detection in complex systems presents significant challenges due to the inherent complexity, high dimensionality, and often unknown nature of system dynamics. Traditional methods frequently rely on reactive pattern matching, which can be easily overwhelmed by noise and fail to capture underlying causal relationships. This paper proposes a novel approach utilizing Causal Bayesian Networks (CBNs) to enhance anomaly detection capabilities. The core idea is to model the system's dependencies and dynamics explicitly using a CBN. Observed data is then used to infer the probability of different system states, allowing us to identify anomalies as deviations from the expected behavior based on the learned causal structure. This approach offers a proactive and robust method for anomaly detection, significantly improving upon the limitations of traditional reactive techniques. The proposed method leverages Bayesian inference to quantify uncertainty and provides a framework for understanding the root causes of anomalies, not just their presence.

title: Rule-based semantic hypergraph parsing from textual annotations
abstract: A semantic hypergraph is a knowledge representation capable of capturing the hierarchical and multi-relational structures essential in natural language. This paper introduces a rule-based semantic hypergraph parser that transforms textual annotations (dependency trees, semantic roles, coreferences) into a semantic hypergraph. The semantic hypergraph parser preserves nested semantic relationships through recursive and ordered hyperedges, integrating predicate-argument structures and coreferences directly into its hypergraph structure. The input textual annotations, the resulting semantic hypergraph representation, and the rule-based transformations applied during parsing are described in detail. The semantic hypergraph parser is evaluated against an existing parser. The qualitative comparison revealed our parser's strengths in handling adverbial modifiers, adjectival clauses, and coreferences. Quantitative evaluation was performed on two datasets: a large-scale corpus of annotated natural language texts, and a manually curated dataset with gold-standard hypergraph annotations. The results show that our parser output achieves almost perfect alignment with gold annotations, outperforming the existing parser by 3–18% on nested representations. After eliminating baseline differences, statistical significance testing confirmed that these improvements were robust across syntactic constructions. We have publicly released our parser to support research on structured semantic representation and to enable practical artificial intelligence applications, including semantic parsing, text mining, and knowledge extraction.

title: An Integrated Video-AI Platform for Action-Level Microanastomosis Training and Performance Feedback
abstract: Developing microanastomosis skill requires repeated practice with timely, action-specific feedback, yet expert review of lengthy microscope videos does not scale to frequent or distributed training. We present an integrated video-AI platform that turns a complete simulated procedure into inspectable, interactive feedback through three connected modules. First, a proposed transformer segments the video into six surgical actions. Second, object detection and tracking localize instrument tips within each action; the resulting kinematic features and action statistics drive supervised classification of five NOMAT-aligned performance dimensions. Third, a grounded large language model (LLM) uses these structured outputs to answer user questions about the current scene, actions, motion, and predicted performance through a unified interface. In a two-site study, 17 participants completed 72 procedures comprising 576 suture placements. The action-segmentation module achieved 87.66\% accuracy and 82.86\% F1, increasing to 93.62\% and 88.32\% after workflow-aware refinement. The five performance classifiers achieved 76.0\% mean accuracy, with Cohen's $κ$ from 0.63 to 0.93. Although the language interface and educational benefit require prospective evaluation, these results establish the technical basis for an expert-supervised platform that can shorten review, expose the evidence behind performance estimates, and support scalable formative microsurgical training.

title: Differential Candidate-Key Contraction in an Experimental GF(101)^4 Feistel Construction: An Empirical Study of Known and Unknown Difference Observations
abstract: We report an empirical phenomenon in which repeated differential observations of a small experimental Feistel construction over (GF(101)) progressively contract a finite population of candidate keys. The construction operates on four field elements using eight Feistel rounds. Four candidate round-function families are defined within the construction; two configurations, denoted (F_0) and (F_1), are examined in detail. Starting from a population of 100,000 candidate keys, known-difference observations reached the planted reference key within three to four observations in the tested experiments. When the input difference was not supplied to the candidate-filtering procedure, substantially more observations were required: in an extended experiment using (F_0), the planted key became unique after 30, 30, and 31 observations for three independent seeds. The (F_0) and (F_1) configurations exhibited similar contraction behavior in the tested experiments. With 20 unknown-difference observations, the numbers of surviving candidates were 31, 21, and 19 for (F_0), and 28, 16, and 30 for (F_1), across three seeds. A reproducibility audit was also performed on an earlier informal record of the experiment. That record reported 23 surviving candidates at observation 20 for one configuration. The current verified reconstruction produces 11 survivors under the same recorded experimental description. The candidate population was verified to be identical to the archived population by SHA-256 hash. An exhaustive local feasibility analysis further showed that 23 survivors cannot be obtained from the verified 29-candidate intermediate state under the verified filtering rule, regardless of which observation values are substituted for the next two observations. We document this discrepancy as a reproducibility issue rather than interpreting it as a cryptographic phenomenon. This report is intended as a dated and citable experimental record.
